paragraph: Ridgefield's single-family market is the core of the activity here, with 23 sales over six months at a median of $720,000, mostly three-bedroom colonials and capes with two full baths. The sale-to-list ratio landed at exactly 1.00 with about 48 percent of homes closing above asking and a median of 26 days on market, so this is competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes are moving, and you should expect competition on the good ones. Two-families are the other real story, and every multi-family sale in the period was a two-family, eight of them at a median of $920,000 with a 1.03 sale-to-list ratio and a median of 14.5 days on market. That tier moves faster than the houses do. Condos and townhouses are thin at six sales, a median of $322,500, and a range running from $225,000 to $935,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Nothing in that tier sold above asking. Monthly counts are too small to read a trend from, including the $920,000 July single-family median off three closings, so use the six-month picture instead. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor is whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the lower price point and low maintenance of a condo.
